question.text: This province is the most populous and borders both Minnesota and New York. The capital Ottawa and the major city of Toronto both lie in this province.
question.clue: The First Nations leader Tecumseh was killed in this province during the Battle of the Thames (TIMS) in the War of 1812.

swap.text: This Canadian province held sovereignty referendums in 1980 and 1995 because many of its residents want to become an independent country. Unlike residents in other provinces, most of its residents speak French.
swap.clue: A Prime Minister from this province signed the Kelowna Accord and passed the Civil Marriage Act legalizing same-sex marriage.

question.leadin: The sign language used by this group is considered severely endangered, with less than forty native speakers worldwide.
question.text: Name this ethnic group that is indigenous to the arctic regions of Greenland and North America. They are known for their use of kayaks and dog sleds in transportation and hunting.
question.clue: In the 1950s, this ethnic group's dogs were killed by the RCMP.

swap.leadin: This party was led by Edward Heath in the early 1970s.
swap.text: Name this party founded by Robert Peel that feuds with the Labour Party.
swap.clue: One member of this party cited an old woman who refused to lease to immigrants in his Rivers of Blood speech.

question.leadin: This man established a provisional government that tried and executed Thomas Scott, after which the Wolseley Expedition was dispatched to put down a rebellion led by this man.
question.text: Name this Metis leader who instigated the Red River Rebellion in 1869. This man was hanged after he led the North-West Rebellion in 1885.
question.clue: This man was captured with the Cree Chief Poundmaker during the Battle of Batoche, and he appointed a tribunal which sentenced Thomas Scott to death.

swap.text: This British major general died after being shot three times during the Battle of the Plains of Abraham. This "Hero of Quebec" was memorialized in a painting by Benjamin West.
swap.clue: This man's second-in-command, Robert Monckton, was wounded in a battle that paved the way for George Townshend to accept the surrender of a French colonial stronghold.

question.text: This 1759 battle in Canada was a major victory for the British even though it saw the death of General James Wolfe. The French general Louis-Joseph de Montcalm also died here.
question.answerHtml: Battle of the Plains of Abraham [accept Battle of Quebec]
question.answer: Battle of the Plains of Abraham
question.clue: It resulted in the death of both commanders: for the French, the Marquis de Montcalm, and for the British, James Wolfe.

swap.text: The nickname "Old Ironsides" came from now-captain Isaac Hull's victory over the Guerriere at the start of the War of 1812. The Guerriere had been heading for this British Atlantic port, now the capital of Nova Scotia.
swap.clue: During the French and Indian War, the British army kept prisoners on Georges Island in this city's harbor.

question.text: After De Gaulle blurted out "Vive le Quebec libre!" at Montreal's Expo 67, this Nobel-winning Liberal Canadian Prime Minister responded, "Canadians do not need to be liberated."
question.clue: This successor to Louis St. Laurent as party leader accepted the Bomarc missile program and instituted universal healthcare.

swap.text: Some Haudenosaunee believe "Iroquois" to be derived from the language of this tribe. This tribe fought the Haudenosaunee in the Beaver Wars and name a lake whose Manitoulin Island was sacred to the Anishinaabe.
swap.clue: Many of these people banded together with the related "Tobacco People," or Petun, after a 1648 attack that killed the Jesuit Jean de Brebeuf.

question.leadin: This man cryptically replied "just watch me" when asked how far he would go to stop terrorism.
question.text: Name this Prime Minister whose time in office saw the October Crisis and the passage of the Official Languages Act, which gave official recognition to both French and English.
question.clue: Peter Lougheed ("LAW-heed") opposed this leader's National Energy Program, which fixed prices after his country weathered two oil crises.

swap.leadin: Name these explorers of the New World.
swap.text: This French dude was the first explorer of the Gulf of St. Lawrence and discoverer of the St. Lawrence river.
swap.clue: On their second voyage, this person made contact with the residents of the village of Stadacona.

question.text: Rupert House in Waskaganish ("VAHSS-kah-gah-NEESH"), Quebec was the first fur trading post created by this company, which founded York Factory. The North West Company merged with this company after the Pemmican War.
question.answerHtml: Hudson’s Bay Company [or HBC; or Compagnie de la Baie d’Hudson; accept The Bay or La Baie; accept Hudson Bay Company]
question.clue: This organization used colored stripes to indicate size and value on its namesake woolen "point blankets".

swap.text: This Canadian prime minister's interior minister Clifford Sifton encouraged Doukhobor emigration in the early 19th century. This first Francophone prime minister passed the Naval Service Bill in 1911.
swap.clue: This replacement of Charles Tupper created his nation's "tin pot" navy when he signed the Naval Service Bill.

question.leadin: These people may have inspired the tuniit("toon-EAT"), a race of giants in a successor culture's mythology.
question.text: Name this archaeological culture, which preceded the Thule people in northern Canada and Greenland. Bows and arrows are conspicuously absent from their sites despite their use by the previous Saqqaq ("sah-KAHK") culture.
question.clue: X-shaped incisions on figures' heads from this culture have been linked to shamanistic travels.

swap.leadin: It was the fifth of a series of acts in response to which the Petition of the King was written.
swap.text: Name this act, one of the Intolerable Acts, that extended one North American colony's domain into the Indian Reserve and guaranteed the free practice of Catholicism in that colony.
swap.clue: Considered one of the Intolerable Acts was this unrelated act that established an administrative system for the namesake French-Canadian province, guaranteed freedom of worship for Catholics, and extended its territory to the Mississippi and Ohio rivers.

question.leadin: Answer the following about strained racial relations in Canadian history.
question.text: This militantly anti-English group's killing of Pierre Laporte in 1970 led to the October Crisis, in which Pierre Trudeau deployed military forces to restore order.
question.answerHtml: FLQ [or Front de libération du Québec; or Quebec Liberation Front]
question.clue: The (+) South Shore Gang was a subgroup of this organization, members of which kidnapped James Cross and Pierre Laporte in an action that prompted Pierre Trudeau to invoke the War Measures Act.

swap.text: During Mulroney's tenure as Prime Minister, he signed the Meech Lake Accords with this man, the Premier of Quebec.

question.text: This Canadian Prime Minister attended the joint funeral for nine of the women killed in the massacre. This man met with Ronald Reagan at the infamous "Shamrock Summit."
question.clue: While prime minister, this man attempted to negotiate a series of amendments which would give increased provincial powers to Quebec.

swap.text: This founder of the Parti Quebecois is considered the spiritual father of the sovereignty movement. Noted for his ubiquitous comb over, he opposed Robert Bourassa, his predecessor in the position of Quebec's premier, during the October Crisis.
